I loved this game. It had the puzzley, voyeuristic elements that I really enjoy from this kind of thing, but also drew on a lot of theory (Baudrillard, gothic social media) that I'm really interested in academically. The game was well put together and the controls were very intuitive. I felt like I always knew what I was doing without feeling like my hand was being held. Although a couple of them created a nice sense of atmosphere, I did feel like some of the jump scares weren't necessary and didn't actually make sense in terms of the narrative. I will definitely be picking up the sequel!

I've never played a game quite like this before, and for that alone I will recommend it. You basically have the phone of a missing girl and attempt to rescue/find out what happened to her by snooping through her phone. You slowly get access to more and more features of her phone (sometimes in really clever ways, like figuring out her password to an app). Slowly a horror plot unfolds as you find out more and more about what happened.

The acting in the game... is pretty amateurish. Plus there are a few far fetched events that take place. But overall the story is compelling enough, and the gimmick of the entire game being played as going through someones phone well done enough, that you still get sucked in.

There are multiple endings, and to get the best endings (as is usually the case) you will have to play through multiple times to see everything. Luckily the speed things up for your second+ playthroughs. Also the horror never really gets too scary, but it does get a bit creepy at times.

Overall definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys video games that push the medium a little.

A decent puzzle type game. While there are the occasional mild jump scares and something strange going on, it didn't really give me a horror or suspense vibe.

Pros:
- I generally stay away from FMV games, but the actresses & voice actors are actually pretty good
- The puzzle difficulty is OK for the most part
- Several other easter eggs and hidden puzzles if you want an extra challenge
- Has a mode for replaying to make text speed up instead of being at a realistic speed

Cons:
- Lacking in horror, and didn't feel that suspenseful
- Texts and responses when texting are often not quite right - grammatically wrong or just don't completely make sense. It could have used some more polish.
- Setting aside the fact that you're going through a stranger's phone instead of giving it to the police/family/etc, there are still things you have to do to progress the story that I would never think to do IRL
- While you frequently have different options for responses to messages, responses to what you say are frequently reused, giving the illusion of more choice than you really have. Good for role playing, but noticeable when replaying
- Has mutually exclusive achievements and different endings, but lacks replayability. Yes you can choose different dialogue option that can influence people differently, but the puzzles and their solutions are still the same.
- I wasn't a big fan of the ending. It didn't make much sense and wasn't really explained. That may have been saved for the second game though.

Verdict: 7/10

If you like eerie, cerebral horror, I highly recommend Simulacra, especially in a bundle with its sequel.  Things you get: 
* A new kind of evil
* Choices that matter (multiple endings)
* A very believable phone to snoop through.   The photos and other clues all blend extremely well with what you'd expect out of a typical phone. 
* Puzzles to solve, with clues often embedded into the content in ways that are not painfully obvious
* Identity theft for a good cause. 
* Both likable and unlikable characters

The only downsides here are that some of the acting quality is kind of meh, but it's an indie game, Play at night with the lights off.  This is a suspense-thriller, not a jumpscare horror-fest, so while there are a few "gotcha" moments, it is the subtle creepy stuff that will get to you.  Best played without "scouting" the plot online first; the villain reveal is much more interesting this way. 

There is also a Free to Play demisequel called Simulacra: Pipe Dreams, so if you're going for the complete collection, you need this, Simulacra 2, and Pipe Dreams.

I am late as hell but wow, I gotta say it doesn't matter what time you decide to play this game.  If you like Psychological Horror games then this is one to check out.  It's dirt cheap at only 5 bucks (2.24) at the time of this review.  I have always been a fan of investigation games and this one is unique in it's delivery.  Putting you in control of a missing girl's phone to slowly uncover what happened or what is happening to her is one of the best experiences I have had in a while.  This game records your choices and all of them affect the outcome of the ending you get.  There are multiple endings so don't just stop at one play through.  It even tells you what percent of the players made the same decisions that you did, similar to how games like Telltale's The Walking Dead or Life Is Strange do it.  If you are a fan of detective games and psychological horror games.  You owe it to yourself to at least try Simulacra.  My first play through took me about 3.6 hours and that was me trying to do just about everything.  I am definitely going to be going at it again to see the other endings

For full transparency: I got this game in a Humble bundle worth 0.99 cents along with 1 other game.

[b][u]The good[/u][/b]
This game has an engaging story, I was seriously invested in the characters and how this was gonna play out. The characters really had a personality to them. The performance of the person playing Anna in particular was great! 
I liked the piecing together aspect this game had and how you slowly uncover more. It managed to hold my attention, for sure. It took me on a ride that I really enjoyed.
You can see that there was a lot of time and effort put into this game, with all the different things that are on the phone and all the conversations that play out. The little image and word puzzles were a nice touch, too. The game looks good and for the most part sounds good, too. 


[b][u]The bad[/u][/b]
The big reveal at the end of the game was… meh. The mystery to the game was much more fun than the answer to that mystery. Although I did like the endings themselves and their ambiguity.  
There were some repeated grammar mistakes that took me out of the experience. Yes, it’s texting, but I feel like in texting you get more typos and less grammar mistakes. The game would benefit from fixing some of these.
The voice acting was a bit spotty. Some actors did a good job, like the detective or Taylor. However, there was one audio clip of Ashley that felt immersion-breaking to me, and Greg in general didn’t sound good to me at all, it was way over the top.

[b]I encountered a game-breaking bug.[/b] For some reason, if you go in the web browser and go to the history section, all web pages that you should only be supposed to look at later in the game are already available. If you read these, events will trigger and the game will think you’re already at those points. The game then runs both the conversations you were already having and the “new” conversations which completely breaks your savefile. So, until this bug is fixed, [b]don’t look at anything in the history section of the web browser[/b].

[b]TL;DR Nice game, I definitely recommend it! But beware of the bug I talked about ^[/b]

The riddles are great (I especially enjoyed the one where I had to find cassie’s phone number), the smartphone control is smooth and realistic, the chats are interesting and humorous, and the story was compelling.
